subject: VPC pricing: blended credits & ops support split
messages:
From: Thomas Green <thomas.green@medisys.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medisys.io>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:12:00Z
Subject: VPC pricing clarification, platform fee amortization and support tiers

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is broadly positive about Redwood's runtime and the private deployment model. Before we move to procurement, we need a clearer picture on how you expect the economics to work for a 3-year deployment across a 3-site EU footprint: specifically:

- How the platform fee is typically amortized (annual vs. upfront) and whether you offer blended-credit structures for rollout phases (pilot -> prod -> scale).
- How support tiers map to response/SLO (oncall coverage, severity definitions) and what add-on costs look like for 24x7 oncall.
- Whether you can provide a short pilot credit or implementation credit tied to the first 3 months of usage while we validate throughput.

Can you send a short term sheet with the amortization examples and a proposed discount matrix for a committed 3-year SOW? We have a timeline to finalize procurement terms by end of June.

Also attaching our security questionnaire separately to this thread — we may need a SOC2 snapshot and a list of standard SLAs.

Regards,
Thomas Green
Head of Cloud Procurement
Medisys Health

Attachments referenced: procurement-RFI.pdf (external)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Green <thomas.green@medisys.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: VPC pricing clarification, platform fee amortization and support tiers

Hi Thomas — thanks for the clear list. High level answers here and I attached a short term sheet that shows worked examples.

Quick summary:
- Platform fee amortization: we support both options. Typical approach is annualized platform fee billed quarterly (preferred for finance predictability). We can also structure a portion as an upfront deployment fee (one-time) with the remainder annualized. Example in attached: 30% upfront, 70% annualized across 3 years (spread quarterly).

- Blended credits: yes — for rollout we offer a staged credit schedule: pilot (100% implementation credit up to X hours + 2 months runtime credit), prod (tiered credits as you ramp commit), scale (discount ladder tied to committed throughput). The term sheet includes a pilot credit line item and a sample blended-credit table.

- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24h ticket TTR), Enterprise (24x7 oncall, 1-hour P1 response, dedicated TAM). 24x7 oncall is an add-on and typically priced as a % of committed platform fee for the year (example: 12–18% for full 24x7 with SRE oncall rotation).

Attachments: Redwood_VPC_Termsheet_v3.pdf (term sheet with amortization examples), SOC2-summary.pdf (cert snapshot).

Next steps: can we schedule a 30–40 minute procurement sync this week to walk the amortization/discount table with legal? I'm free Thu 10–12 CET or Fri 14–16 CET.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Green <thomas.green@medisys.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: VPC pricing clarification, platform fee amortization and support tiers

Hi Thomas — copying in legal/solutions notes that are relevant for procurement. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Contract/License model: We usually propose a node-based license for on-prem with an option to convert to a blended node+seat model for customers who want user-metered admin access. We can show both P&L examples — node-only tends to be simpler for infra-owned deployments.

- Platform fee treatment: If Medisys prefers CAPEX treatment, we can explore an upfront invoice for the deployment component + quarterly invoices for the running platform fee so your accounting can amortize on your terms. We'll flag this as an invoice-option in the term sheet.

- Discount thresholds: For a 3-year, multi-site EU commit we can offer an escalator: 12% list discount at signature, 18% at 12m cumulative commit, 24% at 24m cumulative commit (these are examples; final numbers require visibility on committed baseline tokens/throughput).

- Legal redlines: please expect standard items back from legal — we cannot accept unlimited indemnities or full-source escrow without separate negotiation. We'll attach a redline template.

Action items for procurement call:
1) Confirm desired invoice treatment (upfront vs. annualized).
2) Provide a high-level committed throughput estimate for the 3-year term (tokens/day or P50 latency targets by route).
3) Confirm pilot credit ask (hours & months) so we can finalize the term sheet numbers.

I've attached an editable redline (redline_contract.docx) and the term sheet Ben referenced. If you want, we can join the call and run the amortization scenarios live.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redline_contract.docx (editable), Redwood_VPC_Termsheet_v3.pdf

Ben / Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. A couple of quick confirmations before the call: 

- We prefer upfront treatment for the deployment piece (CAPEX) and quarterly billing for the running platform fee — that approach would align with our finance policy.
- For the pilot credit, we were hoping to secure: up to 120 engineering hours of implementation credit + 2 months runtime credit capped at the equivalent of €25k. Are those numbers we can model in the term sheet?
- We will provide a conservative throughput estimate (tokens/day) by EOD Monday to feed the discount schedule.

We'll take Thu 10:30–11:10 CET for the procurement sync (fits your window). Please send a calendar invite with a short agenda and the DocuSign-ready term sheet, and we'll have legal on the call.

Appreciate it — talk Thursday.

Regards,
Thomas
